newsitem.title: ITALY: All Italian parties urged to back Albania force.
newsitem.headline: All Italian parties urged to back Albania force.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi appealed on Tuesday to all parties in Italy's parliament to back the deployment of an Italian-led multinational force in Albania.
Addressing the Senate (upper house) before the first of two votes on a mission that has caused political turmoil in Italy, he said failure to go ahead would dishonour the country.

"The government is asking the whole parliament to support the effort that this country is being asked to make," Prodi said. "It is not rhetoric but the pure and simple truth to say that the whole world is watching us," he said.
"The Albanian issue cannot be transformed...into an opportunity for a domestic political conflict," he said.
Prodi has run into political trouble over the force after the refusal of the hard left Communist Refoundation party, a key parliamentary ally, to vote in favour of deployment.

Prodi has a majority in the Senate without Refoundation but not in the Chamber of Deputies. The lower house is due to vote on Wednesday and the government may find itself forced to back an opposition motion to ensure the force wins approval.
